newsitem.title: CHINA: China May CPI up 2.8 pct yr/yr-Statistical Bureau.
newsitem.headline: China May CPI up 2.8 pct yr/yr-Statistical Bureau.

text.p: China's consumer price inflation in May rose by a year-on-year 2.8 percent and down from an increase of 3.2 percent in the previous month, the State Statistical Bureau said on Wednesday.
Consumer price inflation for January-May rose by 4.3 percent year-on-year, it said. That compared with a year-on-year increase of 4.7 percent in the first four months.

The consumer price index showed food prices in May had fallen by 0.3 percent compared with the year-ago period while prices of transport and communications equipment fell by 2.6 percent year-on-year, it said.
However, the cost of services soared by 16.5 percent year-on-year and housing increased by 8.2 percent, it said.
Benchmark retail price inflation for May rose by 0.8 percent and by 2.0 percent for the first two months.

China has set a target of 6.0 percent for retail price inflation this year, down from6.1 percent last year and 14.8 percent in 1995. However, officials have said the figure could be 3.0-4.0 percent for the year.
